rationale: Orientation turn on the captured etcd-raft snapshot (go.etcd.io/raft/v3, commit b867cf13f6bc0dae21204302df97bc2355c3af55, CHANGELOG places it just after PR370/PR397/PR414). I read the decision-formation and authority-transition code end to end (raft.go Step/stepLeader/stepCandidate/stepFollower, campaign/poll/reset/become*, applyConfChange/switchToConfig/restore, tracker Progress/QuorumActive/TallyVotes, quorum majority+joint, confchange Changer/Restore, log.go/log_unstable.go, read_only.go, node.go/rawnode.go, storage.go/bootstrap.go, doc.go/design.md) and verified the captured tree against the controller's per-file sha256 record (0 mismatches, no extra/missing files). Local construction feedback only: the repo's own focused selections pass - interaction traces (TestInteraction, 28 testdata scenarios incl. campaign, confchange v1/v2, checkquorum, prevote, forget-leader, snapshot, async-storage-writes ABA), read-index selections (TestReadOnlyOptionSafe/Lease/WithLearner/ForNewLeader/DuplicateRequest, TestRaftFreesReadOnlyMem, TestNodeReadIndexToOldLeader, TestRawNodeReadIndex), and quorum/confchange oracles (quorum TestQuick 50k quickcheck vs reference, TestDataDriven, confchange TestConfChangeQuick/TestConfChangeDataDriven/TestRestore). Those runs are native local feedback only and are not offered as formal evidence. I did not find a source-level contradiction yet, so no defect is asserted; the records below capture the durable behaviors I now rely on plus the two sourced questions (with discriminators) I will take up next, one of them on a guard that no existing test references directly.

investigations.question: In this snapshot, ReadOnlySafe confirmation is count-based rather than commit-index-based (read_only.go addRequest/recvAck/maybeAdvance/heartbeatCtx with confirmedReads, driven from stepLeader MsgHeartbeatResp and sendMsgReadIndexResponse). Which conditions establish that a released ReadState carries an index at least as new as the commit index at the moment the request was admitted, and what happens to still-unconfirmed reads when the leader's term changes (reset() rebuilds readOnly) or when the leader is a fresh leader that has not yet committed an entry in its term (pendingReadIndexMessages)?
investigations.hypothesis: A released read index is never smaller than the commit index recorded at admission of that read request, because positions are monotonic counts and acks are per-voter maxima; the open risk is a lost completion (request dropped by reset/term change) rather than a stale index.
investigations.discriminator: Drive a real 3-node cluster in one process: elect a leader, admit a read request (MsgReadIndex via Step), delay only MsgHeartbeatResp so no quorum ack exists yet, then remove the leader (isolate) and elect a new leader that commits an entry. Deliver the delayed heartbeat responses to the stale leader and record every ReadState and every dropped request. Expected if the count-based claim holds: no ReadState is emitted whose Index is below the commit index at admission; expected counter-shape: an emitted ReadState with a too-small Index (stale read) or a request that is silently never answered after the leader's term changed (lost completion).

investigations.question: hup() refuses to campaign whenever hasUnappliedConfChanges() is true, i.e. whenever any entry in (applied, committed] is an EntryConfChange/EntryConfChangeV2, and promotable() additionally vetoes campaign while an unstable or in-progress snapshot exists. No existing test references hasUnappliedConfChanges directly. Which permitted histories leave a node with committed-but-unapplied configuration entries, and can such a node campaign with a voter set that does not include its own committed configuration (for example after restoring a snapshot, after ReadIndex-style lag in application, or when the application rejects a config change by zeroing NodeId)?
investigations.hypothesis: The guard is a deliberate safety measure (campaign only with an applied configuration) and is correct for the paths it covers, but its interaction with (a) applied<committed gaps created by the application, (b) MsgTimeoutNow-triggered campaigning, and (c) restore/bootstrap paths is untested and may either block a legal transfer or admit a campaign with a stale voter set.
investigations.discriminator: Construct a voter whose storage holds a committed EntryConfChangeV2 that the application has not applied (Config.Applied below committed) and whose stored ConfState predates it, then (i) tick into an election timeout and (ii) deliver MsgTimeoutNow, and read back whether it becomes candidate, which voter IDs it addresses in the MsgVote/MsgPreVote messages, and which quorum quorum.VoteResult uses; the alternative outcome to distinguish is a campaign that proceeds despite the unapplied change, or a permanent inability to campaign after the application refuses the change.

knowledge.statement: campaign() enumerates only r.trk.Voters.IDs() and sends the self-vote as a self-addressed MsgVoteResp/MsgPreVoteResp through r.send, which routes vote responses into msgsAfterAppend so the self-vote is counted only after the term/vote is durable; poll() records the first vote seen per ID via ProgressTracker.RecordVote and TallyVotes returns Voters.VoteResult over the joint config, so a joint quorum requires a majority in both halves and learners or IDs outside the config contribute no votes.
knowledge.conditions: State machine in StateCandidate/StatePreCandidate after campaign() or campaignPreElection(); CheckQuorum/PreVote per Config.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe read confirmation is count-based: readOnly.addRequest appends the request with the commit index observed at admission, heartbeatCtx encodes confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) as an 8-byte little-endian position, recvAck stores per-voter maxima of echoed positions (including the leader's own ack taken immediately in sendMsgReadIndexResponse), and maybeAdvance releases a prefix of unconfirmedReads only when quorum.CommittedIndex over those per-voter positions covers it. The leader postpones MsgReadIndex into pendingReadIndexMessages while it has not committed an entry in its current term, and reset() (any term change) discards readOnly together with all unconfirmed reads and acks.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlyOption=ReadOnlySafe on a leader; the release happens in stepLeader's MsgHeartbeatResp path after readOnly.recvAck.

knowledge.statement: hup() returns without campaigning when the node is unpromotable (not in the progress map, learner, or holding an unstable/in-progress snapshot) or when hasUnappliedConfChanges() finds an EntryConfChange/EntryConfChangeV2 in the index range (applied, committed]; the same guard therefore also applies to the leadership-transfer path, which reaches campaign() only through MsgTimeoutNow -> hup(campaignTransfer).
knowledge.conditions: Any MsgHup, whether from tickElection or from MsgTimeoutNow on a follower, at the term and log state of the node.

gaps.question: Is an unconfirmed ReadIndex request answered, dropped, or answered with a stale index when the leader loses its term between admission and quorum acknowledgement, and which of those outcomes is observable from the ReadState stream?

With a committed-but-unapplied conf change in the log, does the node refrain from campaigning (and if so, is a later campaign possible once application catches up), and which voter set would a campaign use if it did proceed?

interpretations.rationale: Source-only reading of the count-based read-only flow. Positive part: positions are monotonically increasing counts (never reused for a later batch), acks are maxima, and a released read carries the commit index recorded at admission, so a confirmed read cannot be justified by acknowledgements collected for an earlier request; the leader's own ack is the admission position, so a majority echo is still required for confirmation, and pendingReadIndexMessages are answered only after the leader commits in its term, which can only raise the emitted index. Unresolved part: the term-change path. reset() replaces r.readOnly with a fresh instance (unconfirmed reads and acks dropped) while r.readStates is untouched, and releasePendingReadIndexMessages only replies when committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds. I have not yet observed whether a read admitted just before a term change is dropped silently (a lost completion under a legal trigger) or answered later; the snapshot's own TestReadOnlyDuplicateRequest covers only the duplicate-ctx/delayed-heartbeat case and asserts indices are not too small, not that every admitted request completes.
counterevidence: The repo's own read-index selections (TestReadOnlyOptionSafe/Lease/WithLearner/ForNewLeader/DuplicateRequest, TestRaftFreesReadOnlyMem) pass in native local feedback, and TestReadOnlyDuplicateRequest explicitly asserts no too-small read index under delayed duplicate requests plus a leader change, which weakens the stale-index side of the suspicion.
limitations: No retained execution receipt yet: the local test runs are construction feedback and cannot establish a formal conclusion.

Doc.go's Ready/Advance contract does not state that every admitted ReadIndex request must be answered, so a dropped request would have to be argued as a bounded-liveness consequence of an actual trigger rather than a contract violation.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only reading of the campaign admission guard. hasUnappliedConfChanges scans (applied, committed] with pagination and returns true on the first conf-change entry; hup() then refuses to campaign, and promotable() independently refuses while a snapshot is pending/unstable. The guard is consistent with doc.go's statement that configurations take effect when applied, and with applyConfChange/switchToConfig which only reconfigure on application, so a node that campaigns while lagging application would otherwise campaign with a stale voter set. What remains open is whether the guard is complete for the paths that can present a stale voter set (restore from snapshot with only ConfState initialized, bootstrap with applied<committed, an application that rejects a change by zeroing NodeId, and MsgTimeoutNow where the guard also suppresses a requested transfer), and whether the suppression can be permanent for an otherwise eligible voter.
limitations: No existing test references hasUnappliedConfChanges directly, so its behavior is currently only read from source; it must be probed with a real log/apply prefix rather than asserted.
